details.description: Qwen3.5-9B is a 9-billion-parameter multimodal chat model from Alibaba's Qwen team, released February 2026 as part of the Qwen3.5 family. It accepts text and image input and combines Gated Delta Networks with a sparse Mixture-of-Experts and hybrid attention layers, natively supporting a 262,144-token context window that Qwen states is extensible to roughly 1,010,000 tokens via YaRN scaling. It runs in a 'thinking' reasoning mode by default (toggleable off), is released under the Apache 2.0 license, and Qwen states it supports 201 languages and dialects.
advantages: Scores 82.5 on MMLU-Pro and 81.7 on GPQA Diamond, per the model's Hugging Face card.
Scores 91.5 on IFEval for instruction following, per the model's Hugging Face card.
Scores 70.1 on MMMU-Pro for multimodal reasoning, per the model's Hugging Face card.
Natively supports a 262,144-token context window, extensible to roughly 1,010,000 tokens via YaRN scaling, per the model's Hugging Face card.
Supports function calling and structured/JSON output, per Together AI's serverless-models documentation.
disadvantages: Newly released (February 2026), with benchmark figures reported only by Qwen itself; no independent third-party evaluation was found.
use_cases: Multimodal chat: text and image understanding
Long-document and long-context analysis, up to roughly 1M tokens
Tool use and function calling for agentic workflows

notes: Catalog's 262,144 max_input_tokens matches Qwen's stated native context window exactly; Qwen additionally claims extensibility to roughly 1,010,000 tokens via YaRN, which is not reflected in the catalog figure. Modality (image_input plus text) matches Qwen's own 'image-text-to-text' classification. Qwen's model card also describes video input support and reports a VideoMME benchmark score (84.5); the catalog's modality facts list image_input but not video_input, so the video-input claim and the VideoMME score were removed rather than claimed here. Languages were given only as a count (201 languages and dialects) by Qwen, so the languages list was left empty per instructions.
